cities.blurb: Nepal's capital sits at about 1,400 m in the Kathmandu Valley, with Lalitpur (Patan) across the Bagmati.

stats.note: Nomads.com crowd average, labeled Slow on the city page.

season.title: When to go
season.body: October–December (autumn, per Wikivoyage Nepal) About 1,400 m elevation. Average summer temperature 28–30 °C, average winter 10.1 °C; about 65% of rainfall falls June–August; about 1,400 mm annual rainfall (Wikivoyage). Nomads.com monthly median rainfall peaks at 665 mm in August and is 2–29 mm Nov–Mar. Nomads.com AQI data shows October–May as the worst air-quality months, so the dry season has worse air than the monsoon.

neighbourhoods.note: Kathmandu's backpacker district: 'a maze of alleys crammed with handicraft shops, guest houses, and cafés' whose core is traffic-free (Wikivoyage). Wikivoyage notes virtually all tourist accommodation is in Thamel; Nomadista calls it loud and busy but central.

visa.title: Proposed, not available
visa.body: A digital nomad visa has been proposed. The Kathmandu Post reported that the government's economic reform plan included a five-year multiple-entry visa, for people earning over USD 1,500 a month or holding USD 20,000 in the bank, with health insurance of at least USD 100,000. It was described as expected within a year. It is not available yet.

visa.title: What you can use now
visa.body: As of 26 Sep 2026 the Department of Immigration lists no nomad or remote-work visa. Nomads use the tourist visa: 15 days USD 30, 30 days USD 50, or 90 days USD 125. Extensions are USD 3 per day, with a 15-day minimum, up to 150 days in a calendar year (January–December).

also.source: Department of Immigration, Nepal

sim.title: Ncell TouristPro
sim.body: 7 days NPR 595, 14 days NPR 995, 28 days NPR 1,995. Ncell lists unlimited data and voice under a fair-usage policy. Its own pages disagree on the throttling threshold, so that limit is not stated as one number. Bring your original passport. Tourist plans are for non-Nepalese citizens, sold at the airport, Ncell centres, and online as an eSIM.

sim.title: Nepal Telecom
sim.body: A prepaid SIM is NPR 90 and includes a small starter allowance. Data packs on the official tariff include 5 GB for 7 days at NPR 109 and 20 GB for 30 days at NPR 399. No dedicated tourist pack was found. The registration form has a passport field for foreigners.

tips.title: Cash and ATMs
tips.body: Nomads.com marks both cities 'No, cash only (esp. for foreigners)'. Wikivoyage: not all Thamel ATMs accept foreign cards and most that do charge Rs 650 per transaction; Standard Chartered and Nabil ATMs have the highest limit (Rs 35,000 per transaction).

tips.title: QR payments
tips.body: Since 28 Aug 2025, visitors using Alipay+ wallets (Alipay, KakaoPay, GCash, Touch 'n Go, AlipayHK, TrueMoney, Tinaba; 11+ countries including China, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand, Germany and Italy) can scan and pay at eSewa Business / Fonepay QR merchants. Indian visitors can pay the same QR codes with UPI apps (PhonePe, BHIM, Google Pay).…
tips.source: eSewa Blog – eSewa enables international payments via Fonepay & Alipay+

also.source: Techmandu – Fonepay, Alipay Plus launch QR payment for tourists in Nepal
eSewa Blog – Cross-border payment feature (Fonepay + NPCI)

tips.title: Paying a visa fee
tips.body: DoI accepts ETA/visa-fee payment via mobile banking, ConnectIPS, eSewa, Khalti, debit/credit card, or at the TIA bank counter, and advises carrying some cash. A Way Abroad (Mar 2024) recommends bringing US dollars in cash for the on-arrival fee.
tips.source: Department of Immigration, Nepal – Visa Information

also.source: A Way Abroad – A Digital Nomad's Guide to Living in Pokhara, Nepal

tips.title: Ride apps
tips.body: Wikivoyage: Pathao and Tootle work in Kathmandu and Pokhara but need a Nepali mobile number; inDrive supports international numbers (check the pickup pin). A 2025 Pokhara guide says inDrive only accepts cash. Nomads.com lists Sarathi as the 'Best taxi app'.

also.source: Memoirs of Acacia – A Digital Nomad's Guide to Pokhara
Nomads.com – Kathmandu

tips.title: Air through the year
tips.body: Nomads.com monthly median AQI for Kathmandu is 'bad' Oct–May (107–158 US AQI) and cleanest Jun–Jul (16 and 9); annual average 86 US AQI. Pokhara's annual average is 44 US AQI, with 'bad' months Nov–Feb (102–126). Wikivoyage: Kathmandu air quality 'has been very poor since the 2015 earthquake, particularly around the ring road. Buying a dust mask is advisable.'

also.source: Nomads.com – Pokhara
Wikivoyage – Kathmandu

tips.title: SIM at the airport
tips.body: Tourist SIM counters are between immigration and customs at Tribhuvan International Airport (Wikivoyage); Ncell sells its TouristPro SIMs at TIA and offers tourist eSIMs online.

tips.title: Dashain and Tihar
tips.body: Tiny Living (2026): during Dashain (October) and Tihar (November), most independent cafés close for 2–10 days.

tips.title: QR payments
tips.body: Since 28 Aug 2025, visitors using Alipay+ wallets (Alipay, KakaoPay, GCash, Touch 'n Go, AlipayHK, TrueMoney, Tinaba; 11+ countries including China, South Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand, Germany and Italy) can scan and pay at eSewa Business / Fonepay QR merchants. Indian visitors can pay the same QR codes with UPI apps (PhonePe, BHIM, Google Pay).…
tips.source: eSewa Blog – eSewa enables international payments via Fonepay & Alipay+

also.source: Techmandu – Fonepay, Alipay Plus launch QR payment for tourists in Nepal

tips.title: Ride apps
tips.body: Wikivoyage: Pathao and Tootle work in Kathmandu and Pokhara but need a Nepali mobile number; inDrive supports international numbers (check the pickup pin). A 2025 Pokhara guide says inDrive only accepts cash. Nomads.com lists Sarathi as the 'Best taxi app'.

also.source: Memoirs of Acacia – A Digital Nomad's Guide to Pokhara
Nomads.com – Kathmandu

tips.title: Air through the year
tips.body: Nomads.com monthly median AQI for Kathmandu is 'bad' Oct–May (107–158 US AQI) and cleanest Jun–Jul (16 and 9); annual average 86 US AQI. Pokhara's annual average is 44 US AQI, with 'bad' months Nov–Feb (102–126). Wikivoyage: Kathmandu air quality 'has been very poor since the 2015 earthquake, particularly around the ring road. Buying a dust mask is advisable.'

also.source: Nomads.com – Pokhara
Wikivoyage – Kathmandu

tips.title: Tap water
tips.body: Nomads.com: tap water not drinkable in Kathmandu or Pokhara.
